source: Zhang, Yu, Chong et al. (2026, ICML) Verbalized Sampling: How to Mitigate Mode Collapse and Unlock LLM Diversity
finding: Asking for a set of responses with verbalized probabilities in one prompt restores diversity lost to alignment, without training.
numbers: Creative writing: diversity up 1.6-2.1x over direct prompting; recovers 66.8% of base-model diversity; human-rated diversity (1-4) poem 1.90 direct vs 2.39 VS, story 2.74 vs 3.06, joke 1.83 vs 3.01; human quality scores up 25.7%. Gain larger for bigger models (GPT-4.1, Gemini-2.5-Pro get 1.5-2x the gain of the mini/flash models).
limits: Paper says total compute was controlled in its experiments, but also lists extra tokens and latency as a limitation. No per-run token table seen in the sections read. Weaker models can lose quality.
agent_relevance: A single-prompt 'give a spread of options with their likelihoods' step is a cheap generation-phase operator and the nearest equal-budget test of loose generation (gaps 1 and 8).

source: Zhang et al. (2026) Verbalized Sampling - Sequence baseline and temperature ablation
finding: Listing items one after another in one context ('Sequence') raises diversity less than VS; VS stacks with temperature, top-p and min-p.
numbers: Human diversity: Sequence poem 2.07, story 2.76 vs VS 2.39, 3.06 (joke Sequence 2.93 vs VS 3.01). Temperature swept 0.4-1.4: higher temperature raises diversity at a quality cost; VS is orthogonal.
limits: Sequence listing is the nearest thing here to 'discard the first answers' but was not run with explicit discarding. Only poems, stories, jokes; no AUT. Joke gap is small (2.93 vs 3.01).
agent_relevance: Supports prompt structure over temperature (K15). Gap 3 (explicit discard of first k) is still untested.

source: Zhang et al. (2026) Verbalized Sampling - typicality bias in preference data
finding: Human raters prefer familiar text, so preference training pushes models to the modal answer. This is a bias account of why the obvious answer dominates.
numbers: Typicality bias measured as rater agreement above the 50% chance level on several preference datasets, about 56-61% in the panels read (larger models stronger). Human check: 'typical sample' labelled correctly by 95.8% to 100%.
limits: Only a few preference datasets; correlational; typicality defined by base-model probability, which is a proxy.
agent_relevance: Gives an LLM-side reason for the human 'obvious first' order effect: the modal answer is both most available and most rewarded. Inhibiting the obvious is a counter-bias step.

source: Sen, Chun, Alsagoff et al. (2026) Automated Creativity Evaluation of Language Models Across Open-Ended Tasks
finding: Divergent creativity (semantic entropy) and convergent creativity (task fulfilment, retrieval-based multi-agent judge) are empirically separable in LLMs.
numbers: Three domains (MacGyver, HypoGen, BookMIA). Spearman correlation between semantic entropy and convergent metrics is weak in every model and domain. Semantic entropy vs human pairwise novelty: rho=0.56, above cosine similarity, Self-BLEU, Distinct-n. Inter-annotator Cohen kappa 0.61 in one table.
limits: Convergent scores come from an LLM judge, validated against humans on two of three domains. Weak correlation could also be noise. No two-phase intervention was run.
agent_relevance: Supports treating breadth and task fulfilment as two separate dials needing separate operators (generate, then control).

source: Sen et al. (2026) - scaling, temperature and reasoning effects on divergent vs convergent
finding: Larger and newer models improve convergent creativity but not divergent breadth; reasoning variants help task fulfilment; temperature raises semantic entropy.
numbers: Semantic entropy rises with sampling temperature; divergent score does not scale with model size or recency; convergent does. Reasoning variants beat non-reasoning bases (e.g. Llama 3.3) on convergent measures.
limits: Convergent side judged by an LLM; family comparisons are confounded by training differences.
agent_relevance: Control (reasoning) is cheap to improve; breadth needs a scaffold, which fits loose generation first.

source: Geng, Zhang, Lee et al. (2026) Gacha Decoding: Eliciting Diverse Generations Through Instruction Following
finding: Diversity treated as instruction following: the model plans distinct modes and an external random number generator picks among them. Diversity grows with model capability.
numbers: Up to 2.4x Vendi over the next-best prior approach at equal quality; same number of high-quality modes with 11.0x fewer samples; Opus 4.8 at 256 generations per prompt: 7.1x quality-gated diversity over direct sampling; 4.7x fewer generations than list prompting to reach the same mode coverage (3.5x-3.9x in other tasks).
limits: Preprint (Oct 2026), authors' own evaluation on chat, creative writing, image-prompt planning, protein design. Quality-gated metrics depend on the gate. Not an AUT or brain-linked test.
agent_relevance: An external randomiser breaks the model's own typicality pull. Candidate generation operator and an answer to gap 8 with a sample-efficiency number.

source: Hu, Fu, Wang et al. (2024) Nova: An Iterative Planning and Search Approach to Enhance Novelty and Diversity of LLM Generated Ideas
finding: Iterated plan-then-retrieve cycles (outside knowledge) raise the number of unique novel ideas and avoid the duplicate saturation seen by Si et al.
numbers: Unique novel ideas 3.4x the no-planning baseline; at least 2.5x more top-rated ideas than prior agents in a Swiss Tournament over 170 seed papers; over 80% of ideas unique; human eval: 37.5% of top-4 ideas, 17.53% of worst-4. Ablation: without planning unique ideas at step 3 (44.1) did not rise over step 2 (42.4); with neither planning nor retrieval 25.3 to 30.6 to 31.35.
limits: Ranker and some raters are LLM based; token cost per step not matched to baselines.
agent_relevance: Retrieving weak associates from outside the context is a semantic-control operator (gap 5) and beats plain resampling (gap 3). Gains flatten without planning, a weak signal on alternation count (gap 2).

source: Ismayilzada, Cuomao, Yurshevich et al. (2026, COLM) CresOWLve: Benchmarking Creative Problem-Solving Over Real-World Knowledge
finding: On 2,061 insight-style puzzles with one checkable answer, models retrieve facts but fail to make the non-obvious connection.
numbers: Non-thinking models all under 30% accuracy (GPT-4.1 best); more thinking effort gives more accuracy, GPT-5.4 nearly doubles from no thinking to medium; factual-vs-creative drop from -6.08% (Gemini-3.1-Pro high) to -17.21% (Mistral-Large-3-675B) on English; strongest thinking models lose over 20% from Very Simple to Very Hard.
limits: Answers are canonical, so this tests convergent insight not originality. Contamination risk acknowledged. Gap smaller for best model in Russian (-2.14%, -2.73%).
agent_relevance: Gap 9: a control-like step (more thinking) helps on tasks with a correct answer; the bottleneck is the associative leap.

source: Ismayilzada et al. (2026) CresOWLve - error analysis
finding: Failures are dominated by missing creative connection and clue misinterpretation; hallucination and wrong-reference errors (retrieval failure) are rare.
numbers: Difficulty and accuracy do not correlate with number of domains, semantic distance or atomic-fact count; the factual subset matches the creative subset on retrieval demand yet scores higher.
limits: Error categories assigned by the authors; annotation sample size not recorded here. Differs from the human semantic-control reading (retrieval of weak associates).
agent_relevance: Gap 5: for LLMs the semantic-control analogue is forced cross-cluster linking, not extra retrieval.

source: Huang and Yang (2025) Winning Gold at IMO 2025 with a Model-Agnostic Verification-and-Refinement Pipeline
finding: A separate verifier pass that writes bug reports, followed by revision, lifts hard-proof accuracy, with the same base model as solver and verifier.
numbers: 5 of 6 IMO 2025 problems (85.7%) with Gemini 2.5 Pro, Grok-4 or GPT-5, versus baselines 31.6%, 21.4%, 38.1% (best of 32 candidates). A related agent cited: 94.5% vs base 57.7%.
limits: Tokens not equal to baselines; only 6 problems; no quantitative verifier accuracy reported (authors say it can make mistakes).
agent_relevance: Gap 4: a self-run control pass works when errors are findable.

source: Huang and Yang (2025) - repeated verifier acceptance rule
finding: A solution is accepted only if the verifier passes it five times in a row; reported issues are reviewed in a second step.
numbers: Five verifier runs required for acceptance; loop of verify, review bug report, refine.
limits: No measured false positive or false negative rate. Si 2024 near-chance judging (53.3%) is novelty ranking, not error finding.
agent_relevance: Control quality depends on target: error-finding self-checks can work; novelty self-ranking does not (gap 4).

source: Lloyd-Cox, Chen, Beaty (2022) The time course of creativity: multivariate classification of default and executive network contributions
finding: Abstract-level read. Creative vs non-creative classification over three time phases follows a U shape in both networks; executive beats default early.
numbers: Accuracy highest early, lower mid, higher late in both networks. Executive network significantly above default early; later differences not significant. Default accuracy tracks idea quality most early; executive tracks it least early and more later.
limits: Authors call it tentative; abstract only, sample size not read. Contradicts a simple default-first picture and the salience-first time course of Beaty 2015.
agent_relevance: Gap 6: generate-then-evaluate staging survives, but control is active from the start; the generate pass should not be control-free.

source: Beaty, Cortes, Zeitlen, Weinberger, Green (2021) Functional realignment of frontoparietal subnetworks during divergent creative thinking
finding: Abstract-level read (Europe PMC). In n=171 the two frontoparietal subnetworks relate to default differently at rest, and divergent thinking pushes both toward default coupling.
numbers: n=171. FPCNa positively and FPCNb negatively correlated with default at rest (replicated). During divergent thinking FPCNb-default connectivity reversed to positive and its strength correlated with creative ability.
limits: Correlational; r values not read. Says nothing about the achievement-linked separation result.
agent_relevance: Gap 6: coupling replicated in a sample 7x larger than N=25; supports a controller that cooperates with generation.

source: Sunavsky and Poppenk (2020) Neuroimaging predictors of creativity in healthy adults
finding: Abstract-level read. Pre-registered conceptual replication of earlier creativity predictors across grey matter, white matter and connectivity.
numbers: Creativity broadly predicted by inferior frontal gyrus and inferior parietal lobe features, including IFG-IPL functional connectivity; basal ganglia white matter also generalised. Authors say they consolidated some but not all earlier correlates.
limits: Sample size not read; abstract only. Authors stress most prior predictors came from single, sometimes very small studies.
agent_relevance: Gap 6: a pre-registered result partly supports executive-default cooperation; many other claims did not survive.

source: Marek, Tervo-Clemmens, Calabro et al. (2022) Reproducible brain-wide association studies require thousands of individuals
finding: Abstract-level read. Brain-behaviour associations are smaller than thought; typical samples give inflated effects and failed replications.
numbers: About 50,000 individuals across three datasets; median neuroimaging sample about 25; replication improves as samples reach the thousands; fMRI, cognitive tests and multivariate methods give more robust effects.
limits: General across phenotypes, not creativity specific. Within-person, lesion and intervention designs have larger effects.
agent_relevance: Treat all N=12-35 creativity-network effects as upper bounds (K08).

source: Rosenbaum, David, Kaufman et al. (2025) Scaffolding Creativity: How Divergent and Convergent LLM Personas Shape Human-Machine Creative Problem-Solving
finding: Human experiment with divergent and convergent LLM personas as a two-process coach versus a standard LLM.
numbers: 73 treatment vs 32 control participants; 4 excluded for low engagement. Perceived best persona often differed from objective performance. Idea fluency showed no significant condition difference. Divergent persona raised questioning (p=.034 on one measure, n=59 vs 51).
limits: Human-AI teaming, not model internals; small control group; trait analyses exploratory.
agent_relevance: Do not trust self-reported preference for the generate or control step; measure outcomes.

source: Zhang et al. (2026) Verbalized Sampling - model scale and cognitive burden
finding: Structured output costs quality for small models, but the CoT and multi-turn variants remove the cost on large ones.
numbers: VS-Standard and Sequence lower quality, less so with scale; VS-CoT and VS-Multi reach the highest diversity with comparable or higher quality on larger models.
limits: Quality via rubric judge; creative writing only; tokens not equalised across variants. Prior work (Hu et al. 2024) found complex prompts hurt.
agent_relevance: A generate-then-think variant is the best diversity-quality point: small support for separate passes (gap 1).
